source: Seeded from wip-presentation presentation research and translated reference patterns from cowork design-playground and ai-craft docs.

systems.name: Editorial Signal
systems.visual_thesis: Typography-first, clean, and sharp. Feels like a serious product story with editorial restraint instead of a corporate template.

typography.headline_style: large flush-left serif or high-character sans with short action titles
typography.body_style: tight sans body with high contrast against titles
typography.weight_strategy: few weights, large size jumps, strong left edge

color_system.base: warm paper or soft light neutral

grid_and_spacing.spacing: generous outer margins, tight internal grouping
grid_and_spacing.section_rhythm: hero opener then compressed proof sequences

surface_and_shapes.rules: thin rules and alignment do most of the work

chart_and_table_treatment.charts: clean axes, minimal legend noise, takeaway-led annotations
chart_and_table_treatment.tables: light rules, strong row grouping, no heavy shading

image_and_diagram_posture.images: used as deliberate hero or evidence, never filler

systems.motion_posture: subtle reveal only at section openings or single proof moments
systems.title_behavior: titles should sound like claims, not categories
systems.density_profile: medium density with strong pacing contrast
best_for: external talk with clean visual taste
avoid_when: the audience expects dense operational proof on every slide
heavy tables dominate most of the deck
the organization posture rewards conservative enterprise signaling

systems.name: Operational Clarity
systems.visual_thesis: Proof-first and enterprise-safe, but still modern. Feels credible under scrutiny without becoming old, dense, or visually dead.

typography.weight_strategy: clear role-based weights with limited flourish

grid_and_spacing.section_rhythm: steady information cadence with appendix-ready structure

surface_and_shapes.containers: light cards only where grouping helps reading
surface_and_shapes.rules: subtle dividers and explicit table structure

chart_and_table_treatment.charts: native-feeling charts with clear takeaways and annotations
chart_and_table_treatment.tables: strong headers, restrained zebra or grouped shading, easy scan paths

image_and_diagram_posture.diagrams: structured flows, tradeoff diagrams, architecture or process clarity

systems.title_behavior: titles carry the decision or implication directly
banned_patterns: marketing-style hero slides with no proof
best_for: customer or vendor deck with real proof
internal product or GTM decision review
avoid_when: the job needs theatrical momentum more than scrutiny
the presenter voice is intentionally bold or performative
the deck should feel premium or launch-like first

systems.name: Premium Narrative
systems.visual_thesis: Restrained premium drama with deliberate hero moments. Feels polished, confident, and story-led without collapsing into keynote cliche.

typography.headline_style: large dramatic titles with strong rhythm
typography.body_style: short support copy with generous breathing room

color_system.base: dark ink on warm light or rich dark canvas, chosen per deck
color_system.accent: premium metallic, amber, or deep brand accent used with restraint

grid_and_spacing.spacing: wide margins, big section breaks, selective compression
grid_and_spacing.section_rhythm: builds through reveals and contrast moments

surface_and_shapes.containers: few visible frames, more composition than cards
surface_and_shapes.corners: depends on deck mood, usually soft but not playful
surface_and_shapes.rules: thin premium separators or no visible rules

chart_and_table_treatment.charts: few but sharp, often one-message proof visuals
chart_and_table_treatment.tables: used sparingly, stripped down to essential comparisons

image_and_diagram_posture.images: hero images or product moments only when they carry meaning
image_and_diagram_posture.diagrams: reduced conceptual diagrams, high clarity, low clutter

systems.motion_posture: meaningful reveal rhythm is allowed, but must support comprehension
systems.title_behavior: titles can be more dramatic, but still must make a real claim
banned_patterns: slides that look premium but say nothing
avoid_when: most slides need dense tables or detailed evidence
the audience is highly conservative and formal
the delivery mode is mostly skim-first async review
